column1: # The public calls, handlers, audiences and harness calls of the TypeScript kit
# kits/python) for program protocol 16: typescript.md TS-2 and python.md PY-18 and PY-19,
# with the calls of the page rule table in its second form (page-rules.md RULE-55,
# RULE-110, RULE-114) and of animation (animation.md ANIM-17, ANIM-19).
# Each kit keeps a byte-for-byte copy, pinned by COMMON_FROM in its scripts/check.sh,
# and its tests compare its public interface with it.
# Columns, separated by one tab: what (call, handler, audience, harness, timeline, step,
# the TypeScript kit's name; python, the Python kit's name (the TypeScript name in
# snake_case, a handler with on_ before it); message, the protocol message the entry
# writes or reads, or - for none; arguments, in order, by meaning, or - for none.
# A TypeScript handler's trailing context argument has no Python counterpart (a Python
# handler is a method of App), and the Python kit takes the page entries as its App's
# constructor argument, written App(pages): the two structural differences PY-18 allows.
# A third is ANIM-19's: the TypeScript kit's frame takes the sends as its body argument,
# and the Python kit's frame is a context manager whose block is the body, so an argument
# marked (TypeScript only) is not one of the Python call's.
# A timeline row is a member of the kits' Timeline class (written Timeline(...) for its
# constructor, whose one option is a keyword argument in Python and a field of the options
# object in TypeScript), and a step row a method of the step that at and then answer;
# every step method answers the step itself.
# A builder row is a function of the kit's package (in Python, of the neoteletext_app
# module) that only constructs a rule table's object (RULE-55): it checks nothing and
# sends nothing. A modes row is a method of what the builder modes answers (RULE-110):
# in answers the condition that the mode set's variable holds the mode's number, joined
# by and with the condition given, if one is; enter answers the variable command that
# sets it. Python cannot name a method in, a keyword, so its name there is in_.
# What each builder answers, as JSON: physicalKey {"physical":c}; characterKey {"char":c};
# fired {"plus":k,"fired":f}, k 0 when not given; phase
# and noteOff the same with note_off; modes(v, names): in(name)
# n the name's place in names from 0; a name not in names is an error.
# An input's place in its rule's row set (RULE-37's row) is the input's ruleRow in
# TypeScript and rule_row in Python, beside its rule, tick and target: an input's row
# is already the cell row of a pointer event.
# The harness's viewer calls (viewer, privateViewer, remember, forget, grantState,
# The commands sent directly (localMidi to sequence) write exactly the lines of
# docs/command-lines.jsonl, which each kit keeps a copy of and its tests call: a
# sequence started with no at, or with at null, is written with no at, which is the
# next tick (RULE-103, RULE-114; TODO-6681 item 4), and at is written only when a
# time is given. objectPage's object page is the schema's ObjectPageContent (page,
# s1, global, last, objects), written in that order, its page a number as every
# Each kit also exports the limits of a page's rule table (page-rules.md RULE-57,
# REQ-6608) by the engine's names (MAX_RULES, MAX_RECTS and the rest, and
# TICKS_PER_SECOND), generated from neoteletext_rules::limits at the commit its
# scripts/check.sh names (LIMITS_FROM) and checked against it: they are constants,
# not calls, and are not listed here.
# Renderer parity (neoteletext-common docs/renderer-parity.md PAR-38 to PAR-40; the server's
# schema of neoteletext-app-server 25bc0e7): the audience kept, which only regis,
# regisLinks, regisCursor, naplps, naplpsObjects, naplpsLinks and naplpsCursor take and
# writes connections "kept"; regis and naplps take data as bytes, text written a byte a
# character, or a list of parts, sent as parts; a page description's picture is a field
# of the describe handler's answer, picture, { kept: sub-code } or { language, data,
# objects }, not a call. measurePictureText's options are a text part's language and
# outside. A regis row is a member of the kits' Regis class and a naplps row of their
# Naplps class (written Regis() and Naplps() for their constructors, which take nothing),
# each method appending its commands and answering the builder, but parts, which answers
# the parts regis or naplps takes, and object, which answers a NaplpsObject. An argument
# written options (a; b) is one argument, an object of those optional fields in
# TypeScript and keyword arguments in Python; build is a function the builder hands the
# builder of the contents to. docs/picture-examples.jsonl lists builder calls and the
# parts they give, as the message carries them, which each kit keeps a copy of and its
# tests replay: a call's arguments are given as TypeScript takes them, the options last,
# and its name in TypeScript's form (the Python kit's is its snake_case). A naplps row's
# coordinates are dots of the 480 by 500 teletext raster, written at six-byte operands,
# and text's row (1 to 23) and column (0 to 39) name the cell its field and point are set
# at (neoteletext-common docs/naplps-raster.md RAS-6, RAS-8; program protocol 16, RAS-10).
